decision: no blocker to retaining this source-only design; it is not an implementation or qualification
source_findings: Actual Worker sets write_started before raw socket write and adds Worker in-flight state only after successful write; neither step increments BrokerConn in-flight via send_deadline. Zero counters/read buffers alone are insufficient to establish safe transfer.
Preparing.take_groups does not reset write_started; it records write history until begin resets it, not the exact active-write phase.
The raw Worker fire source does not itself invoke send_deadline or the expiry/reauth checks; this is a source qualification gap, not proof that expired traffic was accepted.
Close marks a flag; TCP release can keep its transport object and descriptor alive; BrokerConn Drop aborts its watcher without joining it. Physical retirement must be witnessed.
V2 requires same physical socket and slot generation for the transfer decision, distinguishes independent sessions, and defines pre-write/partial/in-flight expiry controls.

The two v16 projected mock summaries each have 15 failures; v10 physical-wire evidence remains separate and does not establish the v16 socket timeline. Original end-to-end 450ms test source remains pinned.
control_review_caveats: For control 2, first witness actual admission and the gated Worker write, then stop polling or cancel that admitted caller. A never-polled admission future cannot initiate work and should be a separate no-registration negative.

When implementing, test heterogeneous simultaneously live broker API versions, preencoded request bodies and correlation wrap/late responses, as well as same-address broker replacement and authentication credential rotation.
Keep retained-backing byte-accounting scope explicit; shared or opaque user-owned allocation size and allocator/RSS overhead cannot be inferred from a slice length.
The physical descriptor and SASL controls are specifications; none was executed, and a deterministic first-write clock check is not a proof of remote broker timing.
limitations: No Rust patch, Cargo or native test, real Kafka/TLS/SASL run, performance benchmark or production-readiness claim.
V16 job output is an explicitly unverified bounded projection; the full report artifact was not independently read.
The original 450ms end-to-end performance failure remains unresolved.
